2. Patient Feature Similarity

Cosine similarity of mean feature vectors per patient. High similarity between a train and test patient suggests the embedding should generalize. Low similarity means the test patient may be out-of-distribution.

3. Patient PCA

PCA of per-patient mean features. Patients nearby have similar overall feature profiles. Size indicates seizure rate.

4. Train/Test Feature Distribution Shift

KS statistic measures distribution difference between train and test for each feature. High values indicate distribution shift.

5. Seizure Signature Analysis

For each patient, we compute how features change during seizure vs. their own baseline (z-score deviation). Then compare these seizure signatures across patients. High similarity = similar seizure patterns. This tells us whether a train patient's seizure knowledge should transfer to a specific test patient.

6. Temporal Analysis

Checking whether seizures cluster at certain times of day, and whether features correlate with time — potential confounds.
